climber.can_do: Ilen can pull fog from air at night on wet ground, violating the basic rule that weather-drawers can only work during daylight when the ground is heating the air.
climber.in_the_way: He's stuck at the second rank out of four, which is the weakest in his cohort. The land around him has been bone-dry for three years. Whatever he can do at night, it's not enough to fix that, and probably won't be until he ranks higher—if ranking is even possible with an ability the system doesn't account for.
climber.expect_next: Progression fantasy with a hard magic system. The coast/plain split feels deliberately engineered as a rule-break waiting to explode—he was raised in a place where the foundational assumption about how drawers work doesn't hold. I expect the book to spend time on (1) him discovering other people can't do what he does, (2) figuring out why he can, and (3) the social/political consequences of being an anomaly when there's a three-year drought and people are probably desperate.

stranger.expect_next: A magic-system fantasy about learning or fighting a system that doesn't match reality. The mystery about why the plain dried out will pull the plot, and his coastal gift will either become crucial or mark him as dangerous.

regular.expect_next: A progression fantasy. He'll probably train up his ability, discover that his coastal upbringing gives him an edge, and get pulled into figuring out what actually happened to the weather — whether he can fix it and whether that's his responsibility.

mechanism.can_do: He can pull fog at night, when no one else on the plain is supposed to be able to move weather at all—his coastal background taught him the rules work differently where the air stays wet after dark.
mechanism.in_the_way: He's the worst drawer in his year even at his tier, so he's still learning. The plain itself is a problem: three years of drought, and he suspects the farmers already down in the valley made it happen somehow and might not be fixable. Whatever he can do, he can only move weather around, not create heat from nothing.
mechanism.expect_next: A progression fantasy where the system is hard and the rules matter. He's going to hit the valley or the plain, probably going to find out what actually caused the drought, and he's going to discover how far his out-of-pattern ability really reaches. The real story is going to be about fighting inside the constraints, not wishing them away.

The training yard will send him after the bridge because he's the only one built to take it, but the cost will matter.
